redditch-residents-brockhill-west-600hom.core: Posted in last 7 days Redditch Residents - Brockhill West 600-Home Development Views EDITOR'S NOTE – BROCKHILL WEST: WHAT DO YOU THINK? I popped along to the Brockhill West public consultation event at Redditch United this evening to hear more about the proposals to build up to 600 new homes on the outskirts of Redditch. There was a good turnout, and I spent some time chatting to Redditch residents about their concerns. Almost everyone I spoke to was opposed to the development, particularly the prospect of losing more of our countryside. I heard concerns about wildlife, including reports of badger setts in the area, the pressure on local roads and amenities, and what another 600 homes might mean for existing residents. One young man told me how he had spent much of his childhood playing in those very fields. For him, this wasn't just land on a planning map. It was part of his childhood. And one comment particularly stuck with me: "Once the countryside is gone, it's gone." But I am also very conscious that I only spoke to a selection of those attending, and I'd genuinely like to hear from people on all sides of this debate. The UK needs homes, but where should they be built? Do we have the roads, schools, doctors and other facilities to support another 600 households here in Redditch? What about our wildlife and green spaces? And are there people who welcome these proposals because they believe more housing, including affordable homes, is needed? I'd particularly like to hear from anyone who SUPPORTS the development, as well as those who oppose it. At the Redditch Standard, our job is to listen to our community, ask questions and make sure local voices are heard. So, what do YOU think? Are 600 new homes at Brockhill West what Redditch needs, or should this countryside be protected? Please share your thoughts in the comments, or email me at [email redacted]. I'd love to hear your views, whichever side of the debate you're on. Claire Bullivant Editor, Redditch Standard PS You can also write to the developers at: 18 Bennetts Hill, Birmingham, B2 5QJ. Their consultation ends on 30 November 2026. Redditch Standard

people-living-with-type-1-diabetes-podca.core: Posted in last 7 days People Living With Type 1 Diabetes - Podcast Guests Did you know that November is National Diabetes Month in the United States? And November 14 is World Diabetes Day, marking the birthday of Dr. Frederick Banting, who co-discovered insulin in 1921. To be honest, before November 2011, the only thing notable about November to me was Thanksgiving Day. The rest of the month was about colder temperatures, shorter days, and raking leaves. But on October 4, 2011, my oldest daughter Hannah was diagnosed with type 1 diabetes (T1D) at age 11. And just like that, November (and Thanksgiving Day) took on a whole new meaning for me. In the years since her diagnosis, I've done a lot of fundraising (and cycled a lot of miles) to help find a cure for this disease. I've also worked to raise awareness about T1D, including launching T1D Stories in October 2024 — a podcast to inspire people living with T1D, especially those who are newly diagnosed, and the families supporting them. The message at the heart of every episode is simple but powerful: Living with T1D does not put limits on what you can achieve. Hannah was my first guest, and over the past two years, 11 other remarkable people have shared their stories, insights, challenges, and triumphs on the podcast. Since most of these episodes were recorded before our website and newsletter launched this past June, many people haven't had a chance to hear them. So, beginning today and over the next few weeks, we'll be highlighting each episode individually in our newsletter and on social media. argentinian-immigrant-therapist-and-brea.core: Posted in last 7 days Argentinian Immigrant Therapist & Breast Cancer Survivor - Reinvention At 42, Zulma Williams went back to college to become a therapist. Six weeks after earning her bachelor's degree at 46, she was diagnosed with breast cancer. Her plans for graduate school suddenly had to wait, but Zulma wasn't ready to give up on the life she wanted. Born and raised in Buenos Aires, Argentina, Zulma moved to the United States at 31 with limited spoken English, no guaranteed career, and a determination not to spend her life wondering what might have happened if she'd tried. She learned English, worked her way through unfamiliar cultural expectations, and eventually left accounting to pursue a career helping others. When breast cancer interrupted that journey, Zulma began questioning more than her future. She questioned her treatment options, advocated for herself with her doctors, and changed the question she was asking from "Why me?" to "Why not me?" Her recovery took her back to Argentina, where she reconnected with family and experienced the unexpected loss of her mother. Eventually, she returned to the United States, completed her master's degree at 51, and became a licensed clinical social worker. Today, Zulma is a breast cancer survivor, the founder of Dragonfly Therapy Services, and the host of Keeping It Real with Zulma, The Swearing Therapist. At 60, she packed six decades of her life into six pieces of luggage and moved to Panama to live near the ocean she'd always loved. Through humor, grief, cancer survivorship, career changes, and more than one unexpected beginning, Zulma shares why she believes it's never too late to change direction, ask questions, or build a different life.
